information: Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) Trek is a moderate to moderately difficult trek in the Annapurna Conservation Area of Nepal.
The maximum altitude reached is 4,130 meters (13,550 feet) at Annapurna Base Camp.
The standard duration of the trek is 10 to 12 days, depending on the specific route taken.
The trek passes through diverse landscapes, from subtropical forests to high-altitude alpine terrain and the Annapurna Sanctuary.
additional_information: The trek difficulty level varies based on the route; taking the route via Poon Hill increases duration but is much better for altitude acclimatization.

information: The starting point of the trek is Nayapul (1,070m), which is a 3 to 4-hour drive (65km) from Pokhara.
The ending point is Nayapul, from where trekkers drive back to Pokhara.
The total trekking distance is approximately 75 to 85 kilometers via Poon Hill, or 50 to 70 kilometers on the direct route.
Trekkers walk an average of 5 to 7 hours per day, covering 8 to 14 kilometers daily.
Day 1: Pokhara to Nayapul (drive), trek to Hile (5-6 hours, 12km, 380m climb).
Day 2: Hile to Ghorepani (7-8 hours, 14km, steep 1400m ascent through forest).
Day 3: Ghorepani to Poon Hill (sunrise), then trek to Tadapani (7-8 hours total, 13km).
Day 4: Tadapani to Chhomrong (6-7 hours, 10km, descend 470m).
Day 5: Chhomrong to Bamboo (6-7 hours, 11km, through forest along Modi Khola).
Day 6: Bamboo to Deurali (6-7 hours, 10km, 920m steep ascent).
Day 7: Deurali to Annapurna Base Camp via MBC (5-6 hours, 8km, 900m climb, enters sanctuary).
Day 8: Annapurna Base Camp to Bamboo (7-8 hours, 14km, long 1820m descent).
Day 9: Bamboo to Sinuwa to Chhomrong (6-7 hours, 11km).
Day 10: Chhomrong to Tadapani to Ghorepani (7-8 hours, 15km, 680m climb).
Day 11: Ghorepani to Poon Hill (sunrise) to Nayapul to Pokhara (7-8 hours, 18km, drive to Pokhara).
additional_information: Poon Hill (3,210m) is a key sunrise viewpoint along the route, accessed from Ghorepani via 3,767 stone steps.

information: Major visible peaks include Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South (7,219m), Machhapuchhre (Fishtail, 6,993m), Hiunchuli (6,441m), and Gangapurna (7,455m).
Poon Hill offers a panoramic sunrise view of the full Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges.
The trek follows the Modi Khola river valley and passes through extensive rhododendron, bamboo, and oak forests.
Rhododendrons bloom spectacularly in the lower forest sections between 2,000m and 3,500m during spring (March to May).
additional_information: The path crosses several suspension bridges over the Modi Khola river.

information: Nayapul (1,070m) is the starting trailhead with basic tourist shops and transportation.
Ghorepani (2,850m) is a major Gurung village and the gateway to Poon Hill.
Chhomrong (2,170m) is a large, key settlement with a health post and is the last village before the sanctuary where meat is served.
Deurali (3,230m) is a critical altitude acclimatization stop before base camp.
Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC) at 3,700m is the final overnight stop before reaching Annapurna Base Camp.
Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) at 4,130m offers basic lodges directly inside the Annapurna Sanctuary amphitheater.
additional_information: Settlements above Chhomrong (including Sinuwa, Bamboo, Dovan, Himalaya, Deurali, MBC, and ABC) have basic teahouses.

information: Accommodation is widely available in local tea houses (basic lodges) throughout the entire route.
Tea houses generally offer basic twin-sharing rooms with common toilets.
Western-style toilets are common in lower villages, while squat toilets are typical in higher elevations.
Hot showers (solar or gas-heated) are available below 2,500m for a fee of NPR 200 to 400.
additional_information: Hot shower options become very limited, lukewarm, or cold at higher altitudes (especially MBC and ABC).

information: Tea houses serve traditional meals like Dal Bhat, pasta, noodles, and standard Western items.
Dal Bhat is often served with unlimited refills ('food for infinity').
Above Chhomrong (2,170m), meat consumption is strictly forbidden for cultural/religious reasons, and no meat is served.
Tap water is not safe to drink; trekkers must use water purification tablets, filters, UV sterilizers, or buy boiled water (NPR 100-200 per liter).
additional_information: Food and boiled water costs increase with altitude due to transportation difficulties, costing 2 to 3 times more at ABC than Nayapul.

information: Trekkers must obtain an Annapurna Conservation Area Project (ACAP) permit, which costs NPR 3,000 (approx. $23 USD) for foreigners.
A Trekkers' Information Management System (TIMS) card is required, costing USD 20 for individual travelers.
Permits must be acquired in Kathmandu or Pokhara before starting the trek; passport photos are required.
additional_information: Permit checkpoints exist at Birethanti (near Nayapul) and Chhomrong; you must present printed permits.

information: Mobile network coverage (NTC and Ncell) is available up to Deurali, though it can be weak and weather-dependent.
Wi-Fi is offered in most tea houses up to Deurali for a fee of NPR 300 to 500.
Electricity charging facilities are available at tea houses for a fee of $2 to $3 per device.
additional_information: Wi-Fi is highly unreliable or unavailable above Deurali, and power is mostly solar or hydro-based, so a power bank is recommended.

information: The best trekking seasons are Spring (March to May) and Autumn (September to November) due to clear skies and stable weather.
Winter (December to February) brings freezing temperatures (-5°C to -15°C at night) and potential heavy snow above 3,500m.
Monsoon season (June to August) brings heavy rainfall, slippery trails, and risk of landslides/leeches.
additional_information: Daytime temperatures in spring/autumn are pleasant (15°C to 20°C in lower sections, 5°C to 10°C at ABC), but nights are cold.

information: Basic government health posts are located at Chhomrong and Jhinu Danda.
There are no hospitals, clinics, or advanced medical facilities above Chhomrong.
Severe cases of altitude sickness or injury require emergency helicopter evacuation to Pokhara or Kathmandu.
additional_information: Health posts are equipped for basic first aid only; trekkers should carry their own medical kits.

information: Helicopter evacuation from designated landing zones costs between $3,000 and $6,000 USD.
Trekking insurance must cover high-altitude rescue up to 4,200 meters and helicopter evacuation.
Acute Mountain Sickness (AMS) is a moderate risk above 3,000 meters; gradual ascent and hydration (3-4 liters daily) are critical.
Nepal emergency contacts: Police (100), Tourist Police (1144), Nepal Tourism Board (+977-1-5356909).
additional_information: Designated helicopter landing zones exist in villages like Chhomrong, Deurali, MBC, and ABC.

information: Nayapul trailhead is reached by a 3 to 4-hour drive from Pokhara (65 km) along a mountainous road.
Transportation options from Pokhara to Nayapul include private jeeps ($40-$60 USD) or shared public buses/jeeps ($10-$15 USD).
Helicopters are available for charter return from ABC in emergency situations.
additional_information: Private transport is faster and more comfortable than public buses, which stop frequently.
